body.rationale: Governing IPS is still a draft, so I weight IPS breaches as evidence rather than as hard disqualifiers. I favour candidates that pass every hard limit and hold up under peer review. Resampled efficient frontier is first: it passes all IPS tests, is the most diversified of the compliant return-optimised group (effective N 13.3), and its reviews found no errors in the numbers. The one technical error flagged is a wording inconsistency about gamma, and the main weakness, thin drawdown headroom of -24.3% against the -25% limit, is a known risk. Black-Litterman is second: it is IPS-clean, its numbers reconcile (the intra-category reviewer recomputed effective N), and it is candid about being a tuned point. Its technical error concerns the mechanism description, not the weights. pc_researcher is third: it has the best ex-ante Sharpe among diversified candidates (0.51), a modest backtest drawdown (-10.9%), and a CRO risk of 0.33. Its breaches are volatility and tracking error only, and the reviews show its rationale was not reconciled with the solved result, so I rank it below the two compliant methods. CVaR minimisation is fourth: it passes the IPS, has the best backtest Sharpe among the compliant candidates (0.74), and covers tail risk with a non-covariance approach, so the ensemble gains a different view. Its weakness is fitting to a handful of crises and sitting at the volatility edge. Max Sharpe is fifth: it is IPS-clean, but 46% in us_value rests on one judged CMA gap, as its reviewers noted. Resampled efficient frontier beats max_sharpe because it spreads that estimation risk across draws instead of concentrating in a single style bet. Bottom flag is hierarchical risk parity: roughly 92% in cash and short Treasuries, breaching return, volatility and tracking error together, with a technical error in how its recursion was described and a design choice to treat cash as a risk node. It is the portfolio I would least want the CIO to lean on. I did not flag the adversarial diversifier, since its orthogonality is valuable in an ensemble. I also acknowledge I am a market-cap heuristic with my own drawdown breach, and I voted on merit regardless.
